title: Harassment Prevention Policy

articles.heading: Employer's Context and Intentions
paragraphs: The social context of recent years in Quebec, as elsewhere, has been marked by increased awareness of harassment in general — whether physical, psychological, sexual, or economic in nature — and of the need to act, notably by preventing actions or words that could give rise to harassment. The emergence of the #metoo movement reflects this concern well, inviting anyone, whether a victim themselves or a witness to harassing acts or words, to report such things to the appropriate authorities. The reform of the Act respecting labour standards in Quebec now requires all employers, as of January 1, 2019, to implement a policy to combat workplace harassment in all its forms.

In this context, Cible Retour à l'Emploi's intentions through this policy are also to ensure the health and safety of anyone who is in contact with our organization, regardless of how or with which representative.

articles.heading: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
paragraphs: Anyone who comes into contact with our organization — whether a participant in our services, an employee, a member of management or the board of directors, a supplier, a government representative, or simply a citizen making inquiries about us — is covered by this policy. However, since this is an internal policy governing workplace behaviour, the expectations and related sanctions can only be applied to employees and official representatives themselves; any other person will be referred to Quebec's judicial system.

articles.heading: What Constitutes Harassment?
paragraphs: We define harassment as any action or spoken or written word directed at another person, the purpose of which, apparent or implied, is to harm the other person's privacy or moral, physical, psychological, or sexual integrity in order to gain something for personal benefit, and which occurs repeatedly.

Harassment is assessed based on the perception of the person who feels harassed. This perception must be corroborated by facts and, where applicable, by a neutral witness. Harassment normally results from the accumulation and repetition of several behaviours over a certain period of time, unless a single act is so serious that it alone produces a continuous harmful effect.

Physical harassment includes, without being exhaustive, any repeated, unwanted physical contact intended to provoke, humiliate, intimidate, push, hit, injure, or otherwise harm another person, regardless of the duration of such acts or the place or time at which they occur. Such situations must be reported to executive management, which will see to intervening as appropriate.

This type of harassment is more insidious and difficult to detect but shares the same elements as other forms of harassment: it is directed at a specific person, is vexatious and repetitive in nature, is unwanted, and produces negative and undesirable effects on its victim. Psychological harassment includes, without being exhaustive, any written or spoken action or comment intended to degrade, vex, humiliate, ridicule, hurt, or confuse the other person in order to gain some advantage.

Sexual harassment includes, without being exhaustive, any repeated, unwanted physical contact seeking to establish unwanted intimacy with another person, or any spoken or written word seeking to establish an intimate relationship or describing intentions, fantasies, or obscene acts featuring the victim and their harasser.

Much less well known than other forms of harassment and present especially among seniors, this form is specifically related to money as the coveted object. However, the means used are just as varied as for other forms of harassment: repeated, unwanted, and vexatious actions or words directed at a single individual, with the aim of extracting money from that person or establishing economic control over them.

articles.heading: The Employer
paragraphs: As a legal entity with corporate status, Cible Retour à l'Emploi, as an employer, has the responsibility to: establish a policy to combat workplace harassment; appoint a person responsible for applying this policy; share this policy with its employees and the public; offer support to employees affected by a harassment complaint.

articles.heading: The Chief Executive/Manager
paragraphs: Executive management is responsible for: ensuring healthy and pleasant working relationships among staff; receiving comments and complaints about harassment; guaranteeing confidential handling of any complaint and any statements reported to them; following up on complaints and informing the parties concerned of the results; supporting people who have experienced harassment by referring them, if warranted, to another more appropriate resource; raising awareness among Cible Retour à l'Emploi staff about the effects of harassment.

articles.heading: Cible Retour à l'Emploi Employees
paragraphs: As a representative of their employer, each employee has the responsibility to: help maintain a healthy, respectful, and safe atmosphere both at their workplace and outside of it; comply with this policy; refuse to take part in any act or speech of a hateful, vexatious, or harassing nature; report and bring to executive management's attention any event or fact that comes to their attention involving harassment.

In accordance with the complaint-handling policy adopted in November 2017, anyone may file a complaint with the executive management of Cible Retour à l'Emploi using the complaint form, which is also available at the reception desk and on our website, regardless of whether the complaint concerns the person themselves or another person.
Executive management will ensure confidential handling and follow-up of the complaint, communicating with the individuals concerned only when necessary.
